Anthropic Claude Model Release Timeline - Model Family Tree, Capability Evolution, and Platform Availability | hidekazu-konishi.com hidekazu-konishi.com Profile  |  Privacy  |  Blog   >   Anthropic Claude Model Release Timeline - Model Family Tree, Capability Evolution, and Platform Availability https://hidekazu-konishi.com/images/anthropic_claude_model_release_timeline.jpg Anthropic Claude Model Release Timeline - Model Family Tree, Capability Evolution, and Platform Availability | hidekazu-konishi.com Anthropic Claude Model Release Timeline - Model Family Tree, Capability Evolution, and Platform Availability First Published: 2026-05-16 Last Updated: 2026-07-26 This article is a non-AWS installment in my history-and-timeline series, where I have previously tracked the evolution of individual AWS services such as AWS Lambda, Amazon Bedrock, AWS IAM, Amazon S3, Amazon DynamoDB, and AWS CloudFormation. This time, I have built a complete release timeline for Anthropic's Claude foundation model family, from the original Claude 1 announced in March 2023 through Claude Fable 5 and Claude Sonnet 5 announced in June 2026 and Claude Opus 5 announced in July 2026. I summarize the model family tree of Claude Opus, Claude Sonnet, and Claude Haiku - now joined by the Mythos-class tier above Opus introduced with Claude Fable 5 - the full chronology of major releases with links to the official anthropic.com/news/ announcements, the evolution of capabilities (context window, vision, tool use, computer use, prompt caching, extended thinking, memory tool, 1M context, effort parameter), the differences in availability across the Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry, and the lifecycle of deprecated and retired Claude models as listed on Anthropic's official model deprecation page. Companion articles on hidekazu-konishi.com: AWS History and Timeline regarding Amazon Bedrock - Overview, Functions, Features, Summary of Updates, and Introduction Amazon Bedrock Model Catalog 2026 Claude Code Features and Settings Reference 2026 Overview - From Anthropic's Founding to Claude Fable 5 Anthropic was founded in 2021 as an AI safety company by former OpenAI researchers, and published the paper "Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback" in December 2022 introducing the training method that has since shaped every Claude model. The first publicly available Claude model arrived on March 14, 2023, when Anthropic launched the Anthropic API with Claude and Claude Instant. Three years later, as of the time of writing, the Claude family covers three named size tiers - Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku - introduced together with Claude 3 in March 2024, joined in June 2026 by the Mythos-class tier that sits above the Opus class, with the current frontier being Claude Fable 5 announced on June 9, 2026. Across these three years, Claude has been the first foundation model from a frontier lab to reach a 100K-token context window (May 2023), an early adopter of vision input across all model tiers (Claude 3, March 2024), the launch model for Computer Use as a public beta capability (Claude 3.5 Sonnet new, October 2024), and the introduction point for the extended-thinking and hybrid-reasoning paradigm in a production model (Claude 3.7 Sonnet, February 2025). The 4.x generation that started in May 2025 brought a 1-million-token beta context window, the effort parameter that lets developers trade off speed against capability, an explicit memory tool, and incremental coding gains that have made Claude Opus 4.x the default model for several AI-coding agent products. Claude Opus 4.8 (May 28, 2026) shifts the emphasis toward honesty and reliability - Anthropic reports it is roughly four times less likely than Opus 4.7 to let flaws in code it has written pass unremarked - and ships alongside a Dynamic Workflows research preview in Claude Code that orchestrates hundreds of parallel subagents. Less than two weeks later, on June 9, 2026, Anthropic announced Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5, the first models in the new Mythos-class tier that sits above the Opus class in capability. Claude Fable 5, described by Anthropic as its most capable widely released model with state-of-the-art results on nearly all tested benchmarks, is the generally available Mythos-class model: it runs with always-on adaptive thinking, a 1-million-token context window, and 128K output tokens, and includes safety classifiers that automatically fall back to Claude Opus 4.8 for flagged requests in domains such as cybersecurity and biology. Claude Mythos 5 shares the same capabilities without the safety classifiers and is offered only in limited availability through Project Glasswing. On June 12, 2026, less than a week after this launch, Anthropic announced that it had received a US government export-control directive requiring it to suspend access to both Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5; Anthropic states that complying with the order forces it to disable the two Mythos-class models for all customers, while access to all other Claude models (Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku) remains unaffected and it works to restore access. On June 30, 2026, after the export-control directive was lifted, Anthropic announced that it was redeploying Claude Fable 5 globally (starting July 1, 2026) with updated cybersecurity safeguards, while restoring Claude Mythos 5 access for a set of US organizations. The same day, Anthropic also released Claude Sonnet 5, its most capable Sonnet-tier model, bringing near-Opus intelligence to coding and agentic work at Sonnet cost. On July 24, 2026, Anthropic released Claude Opus 5, a step-change improvement over Claude Opus 4.8 at the Opus tier, described as coming close to Claude Fable 5's frontier intelligence at half the price: it supports a 1-million-token context window (both the default and the maximum) with 128K output tokens, runs with thinking on by default, and became the new default model on the Claude Max plan. The scope of this article is limited to publicly announced models and capabilities documented at anthropic.com/news/ and the official Claude API documentation. I do not include speculative future models. Pricing details change frequently and are deliberately omitted in favor of links to Anthropic's official pricing page. This timeline primarily references the following sources. Anthropic News Claude API Documentation Model deprecations - Claude API What's New with AWS - Amazon Bedrock Claude Model Family Tree (Fable / Opus / Sonnet / Haiku) Since the Claude 3 generation introduced in March 2024, the family has been organized into three named size tiers: Opus (maximum capability), Sonnet (balanced), and Haiku (low latency, low cost). The pre-3 generation (Claude 1, Claude Instant, Claude 2, Claude 2.1) predates this naming scheme; in retrospect, Claude 1 and Claude 2 sit on the Opus lineage and Claude Instant sits on the Haiku lineage. The diagram below shows the full family tree from Claude 1 in 2023 through the Mythos-class tier introduced with Claude Fable 5 in June 2026. Anthropic Claude Model Family Tree (Fable / Opus / Sonnet / Haiku) The Opus lane covers the largest, most capable models: Claude 1 (March 2023), Claude 2 (July 2023), Claude 2.1 (November 2023), Claude 3 Opus (March 2024), Claude Opus 4 (May 2025), Claude Opus 4.1 (August 2025), Claude Opus 4.5 (November 2025), Claude Opus 4.6 (February 2026), Claude Opus 4.7 (April 2026), Claude Opus 4.8 (May 2026), and Claude Opus 5 (July 2026). The Sonnet lane covers the balanced tier introduced with Claude 3: Claude 3 Sonnet (March 2024), Claude 3.5 Sonnet (June 2024), Claude 3.5 Sonnet new / v2 (October 2024), Claude 3.7 Sonnet (February 2025), Claude Sonnet 4 (May 2025), Claude Sonnet 4.5 (September 2025), Claude Sonnet 4.6 (February 2026), and Claude Sonnet 5 (June 2026). The Haiku lane is the fastest and lowest-cost tier: Claude Instant (March 2023, retrospectively on the Haiku lineage), Claude 3 Haiku (March 2024), Claude 3.5 Haiku (October 2024 announce, November 2024 availability), and Claude Haiku 4.5 (October 2025). Note that Anthropic has not released Haiku versions corresponding to every Sonnet/Opus minor revision - Haiku 4.0, Haiku 4.6, Haiku 4.7, and Haiku 4.8 do not exist as of July 2026. In June 2026, the family gained a fourth, Mythos-class tier positioned above the Opus lane: Claude Fable 5 (June 2026) is the generally available Mythos-class model, and Claude Mythos 5 (June 2026) shares the same capabilities without the safety classifiers and is offered in limited availability through Project Glasswing. Timeline of Major Releases Here is the full chronological timeline of Anthropic Claude model releases and major capability announcements. Each row links to the official anthropic.com/news/ post or the equivalent official source. * The table can be sorted by clicking on the column names. Date Event 2021-01 Anthropic is founded as an AI safety company by Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei, and other former OpenAI researchers. 2022-12-15 Anthropic publishes the Constitutional AI paper introducing the alignment method that underpins every later Claude model. Source: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback . 2023-03-14 Claude 1 and Claude Instant are announced and the Anthropic API opens for early access. Source: Introducing Claude . 2023-05-11 The context window is expanded from 9K to 100K tokens on Claude. This was the first 100K-token context window from a frontier AI lab. Source: Introducing 100K Context Windows . 2023-07-11 Claude 2 is announced with improved coding, math, and reasoning, the public claude.ai chat interface, and a 100K context window. Source: Claude 2 . 2023-08-01 Claude 2 becomes available on Amazon Bedrock (in preview) with up to 100,000-token context windows, joining Anthropic Claude as a Bedrock preview model ahead of Bedrock's GA. Source: Anthropic's Claude 2 foundation model is now available in Amazon Bedrock . 2023-09-25 Anthropic and Amazon announce a strategic collaboration under which Anthropic will make future Claude models available on Amazon Bedrock and use AWS Trainium and Inferentia for training. Source: Anthropic + Amazon . 2023-09-28 Amazon Bedrock reaches general availability in US East (N. Virginia) and US West (Oregon) with Anthropic Claude 2 as one of the launch foundation models, alongside models from AI21 Labs, Cohere, Stability AI, and Amazon Titan (with Meta's Llama 2 following soon after). Source: Amazon Bedrock is now generally available . 2023-11-21 Claude 2.1 is announced with a 200K-token context window, system prompts, and tool use as a beta. Source: Claude 2.1 . 2024-03-04 The Claude 3 family is announced (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku), introducing the three-tier naming scheme that all later Claude models follow. Claude 3 is the first Claude family with multimodal (vision) input across every model tier. Claude 3 Opus and Claude 3 Sonnet are available the same day; Claude 3 Haiku follows shortly after. Source: Introducing the next generation of Claude . 2024-03-13 Claude 3 Haiku is generally available on the Anthropic API. Source: Claude 3 Haiku - our fastest model yet . 2024-04-04 Tool use enters public beta on the Claude API, allowing models to call developer-defined functions. 2024-05-30 Tool use becomes generally available on Claude 3 Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku. Source: Tool use is now generally available . 2024-06-20 Claude 3.5 Sonnet is announced with significant gains in coding, reasoning, and vision, and at the same price and speed as Claude 3 Sonnet. The same announcement introduces the Artifacts feature in claude.ai . Source: Claude 3.5 Sonnet . 2024-08-14 Prompt caching enters public beta on the Anthropic API, allowing developers to cache long repeated prompt prefixes for cost and latency reductions. Source: Prompt caching with Claude . 2024-10-08 The Message Batches API enters public beta , enabling asynchronous batch processing of up to 10,000 messages at 50% off standard pricing. Source: Introducing the Message Batches API . 2024-10-22 Claude 3.5 Sonnet (new) and Claude 3.5 Haiku are announced , and Computer Use is released as a public beta capability, allowing Claude to perceive and interact with computer interfaces by viewing screens, moving the cursor, clicking, and typing. Source: Introducing computer use, a new Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Claude 3.5 Haiku . 2024-11-04 Claude 3.5 Haiku becomes available on the Anthropic API. 2025-02-24 Claude 3.7 Sonnet is announced as Anthropic's first hybrid reasoning model with both standard and extended-thinking modes that the user controls via the API, alongside a research preview of the Claude Code command-line coding agent. Source: Claude 3.7 Sonnet and Claude Code . 2025-05-22 Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4 are announced , kicking off the Claude 4 generation. Claude Opus 4 is positioned as the world's best coding model at the time of announcement, with extended-thinking with tool use and improved memory features. Claude Code reaches general availability. Source: Introducing Claude 4 . 2025-08-05 Claude Opus 4.1 is announced with improved coding (74.5% on SWE-bench Verified), research, and data-analysis performance, available on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, and Google Cloud Vertex AI. Model identifier claude-opus-4-1-20250805 . Source: Claude Opus 4.1 . 2025-09-29 Claude Sonnet 4.5 is announced with major coding, instruction-following, and agentic improvements at the same price as Sonnet 4. The same announcement adds a context editing feature and a memory tool to the Claude API. Model identifier claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 . Source: Claude Sonnet 4.5 . 2025-10-15 Claude Haiku 4.5 is announced , the first Haiku model to support both extended thinking and Computer Use. It matches Claude Sonnet 4's coding performance at roughly one-third the cost and over twice the speed. Model identifier claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 . Source: Claude Haiku 4.5 . 2025-11-24 Claude Opus 4.5 is announced with the new effort parameter for balancing capability against cost, context compaction, and a deeper memory tool. Available on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry. Model identifier claude-opus-4-5-20251101 . Source: Claude Opus 4.5 . 2026-02-05 Claude Opus 4.6 is announced , inheriting the 1-million-token beta context window (first introduced on Claude Sonnet 4 on 2025-08-12) at the Opus tier, with 128K output tokens, adaptive thinking, and a new Claude Code "agent teams" feature for parallel autonomous work. Model identifier claude-opus-4-6 (first generation to use the dateless pinned-snapshot ID format). Source: Claude Opus 4.6 . 2026-02-17 Claude Sonnet 4.6 is announced , retaining the 1-million-token beta context window (introduced with Claude Sonnet 4 in August 2025) and adding major improvements in coding and Computer Use. Users preferred Sonnet 4.6 to Opus 4.5 59% of the time. Model identifier claude-sonnet-4-6 . Source: Claude Sonnet 4.6 . 2026-04-16 Claude Opus 4.7 is announced as the frontier model at the time, with substantial gains on the hardest coding tasks, higher-resolution vision input, a new xhigh effort level, file-system-based memory recall across sessions, and the Task Budgets public beta. Available on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry. Model identifier claude-opus-4-7 . Source: Claude Opus 4.7 . 2026-05-28 Claude Opus 4.8 is announced as the new frontier model, roughly 42 days after Opus 4.7 - the shortest gap so far between consecutive Claude Opus releases (versus about 70-75 days for the previous Opus steps). The emphasis is on honesty and reliability (Anthropic reports it is approximately four times less likely than Opus 4.7 to let flaws in code it has written pass unremarked), more efficient tool calling, and better agentic judgment - including stronger computer-use and browser-agent performance (84% on the Online-Mind2Web benchmark, surpassing Opus 4.7) - alongside gains across coding, reasoning, and knowledge work. It launches together with Dynamic Workflows in Claude Code (research preview) - an orchestrator that runs hundreds of parallel subagents that each plan, execute, and verify part of a task - and user-facing effort control for claude.ai and Cowork, plus a fast mode priced about 3x lower than on previous models. Available on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry. Model identifier claude-opus-4-8 . Source: Claude Opus 4.8 , Claude Opus 4.8 is now available on AWS . 2026-06-09 Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 are announced , introducing the Mythos-class capability tier that sits above the Opus class - the first new named tier since Opus / Sonnet / Haiku arrived with Claude 3 in March 2024. Claude Fable 5 is the generally available Mythos-class model, reported by Anthropic as state-of-the-art on nearly all tested benchmarks spanning software engineering, knowledge work, vision, and scientific research, with a 1-million-token context window, 128K output tokens, and always-on adaptive thinking (the thinking parameter cannot be disabled; depth is controlled via the effort parameter). It ships with safety classifiers covering cybersecurity, biology/chemistry, and distillation attempts that automatically fall back to Claude Opus 4.8 for flagged requests (affecting less than 5% of sessions), supported by a new fallbacks API parameter (beta) and fallback credit for retries. Claude Mythos 5 shares the same capabilities without the safety classifiers and is offered in limited availability to approved customers through Project Glasswing. Claude Fable 5 is generally available on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry from day one, and is selectable in Claude Code via /model fable (it is not the default model). Model identifiers claude-fable-5 and claude-mythos-5 . Source: Introducing Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 . 2026-06-12 Access to Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 is suspended under a US government directive . Anthropic states that on June 12, 2026 (5:21pm ET) it received an export-control directive requiring it to suspend access to both Mythos-class models for any foreign national - whether inside or outside the United States, and including foreign-national Anthropic employees - the net effect of which, Anthropic says, is that it must disable Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 for all customers to ensure compliance. The government cited a suspected method of bypassing ("jailbreaking") Claude Fable 5's safeguards, reportedly demonstrated by asking the model to read a codebase and fix its software flaws; Anthropic responded that the technique revealed only relatively simple vulnerabilities that are also reachable through other commercially available models, that it disagrees that a narrow potential jailbreak should be cause for recalling a commercial model, and that it is working to restore access as soon as possible. Access to all other Claude models (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) is unaffected. Source: Statement on the US government directive to suspend access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 . 2026-06-30 Claude Sonnet 5 is announced , described by Anthropic as its most capable Sonnet model yet - bringing near-Opus intelligence to coding, agents, and professional work at Sonnet cost, and a strict improvement over Sonnet 4.6 across the cost-performance curve. It becomes the default model for the Free and Pro plans and is the first Sonnet-tier model with the xhigh effort level and higher-resolution vision. It offers adaptive thinking, a 1-million-token context window, 128K output tokens, and cyber safeguards enabled by default, and adopts the updated tokenizer introduced with Opus 4.7. Available on the Claude API, Claude Code, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry. Model identifier claude-sonnet-5 . Source: Introducing Claude Sonnet 5 , Claude Sonnet 5 now available on AWS . 2026-06-30 Anthropic announces the redeployment of Claude Fable 5 following the lifting of the US government export-control directive. Claude Fable 5 returns globally starting June 30 / July 1, 2026 with updated cybersecurity safeguards - including a new safety classifier that blocks the reported bypass in over 99% of cases - and Claude Mythos 5 access is restored for a set of US organizations (approved on June 26, 2026). Anthropic also proposes an early-draft industry framework for scoring the severity of AI jailbreaks, developed with its Project Glasswing partners. Source: Redeploying Claude Fable 5 . 2026-07-02 Anthropic publishes further detail on Claude Fable 5's cyber safeguards and its proposed jailbreak-severity framework , describing which categories of cybersecurity harm the safety classifiers are and are not designed to prevent, an early-draft severity framework being developed with Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and other Project Glasswing partners, and a HackerOne bug-bounty program for reporting potential cyber jailbreaks in Fable 5. Source: More details on Fable 5's cyber safeguards and our jailbreak framework . 2026-07-24 Claude Opus 5 is announced as a step-change improvement over Claude Opus 4.8 at the Opus tier, described by Anthropic as coming close to Claude Fable 5's frontier intelligence at half the price, at the same price as Claude Opus 4.8. It supports a 1-million-token context window (both the default and the maximum) and 128K output tokens, runs with thinking on by default (disabling thinking is allowed only at effort high or below), supports the full effort ladder ( low / medium / high / xhigh / max ), and offers a fast mode at around 2.5 times the default speed. Its cybersecurity safety classifiers are expected to intervene about 85% less often than Claude Fable 5's, with flagged requests falling back to Claude Opus 4.8 by default in Claude apps, and cyber-related requests blocked on Claude Fable 5 now route to Claude Opus 5 rather than Claude Opus 4.8. It launches alongside two betas - mid-conversation tool changes (change a conversation's tools without invalidating the prompt cache) and automatic fallbacks on the API - and becomes the new default model on the Claude Max plan. Available on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry from day one; the same day, fast mode for Claude Opus 4.7 is removed. Model identifier claude-opus-5 . Source: Introducing Claude Opus 5 , Claude Opus 5 is now available on AWS . There may be slight variations in the dates in this timeline due to differences between announcement, general availability on the Anthropic API, and general availability on cloud platforms. The dates above prioritize the original Anthropic announcement date when both exist. The content posted here is limited to major releases and capabilities considered essential for understanding the Claude family. In other words, please note that the items on this timeline are not all updates from Anthropic, but are representative releases that I have picked out. The first major external platform was Amazon Bedrock, which has carried Claude since the Bedrock general availability launch on 2023-09-28. Note that Anthropic's Claude (the Claude 1 generation and Claude Instant) was already among the launch foundation models when Amazon Bedrock was announced in limited preview on April 13, 2023; the table above uses general-availability dates, which is why the Claude 1 / Claude Instant row shows "-" for Amazon Bedrock. Google Cloud Vertex AI began offering Claude models in March 2024, when Claude 3 Sonnet and Claude 3 Haiku reached general availability there; Claude 3 Opus followed in public preview in April 2024 and reached general availability in June 2024. Microsoft Foundry is the most recent addition: it first carried Claude on November 18, 2025, when Claude Sonnet 4.5, Claude Haiku 4.5, and Claude Opus 4.1 became available in public preview, and it has joined the day-one launches from Claude Opus 4.5 (November 24, 2025) onward. For the most current platform availability and exact regional rollouts, refer to Amazon Bedrock supported foundation models , Google Cloud Vertex AI Anthropic Claude models , and the Microsoft Foundry model catalog . Although Claude Fable 5 became generally available on all four platforms on June 9, 2026, access to Claude Fable 5 (and the limited-availability Claude Mythos 5) was suspended on June 12, 2026 under a US government directive and then restored - Anthropic began redeploying Claude Fable 5 globally on July 1, 2026 after the directive was lifted; see the Frequently Asked Questions below. Access to all other Claude models on these platforms was unaffected throughout. Claude Sonnet 5 launched on June 30, 2026 on the Claude API / Claude Platform (including Claude Platform on AWS), Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry, and Claude Opus 5 followed on July 24, 2026 with the same day-one availability across all four platforms. Deprecations and Model Lifecycle Anthropic operates a four-stage model lifecycle: Active → Legacy → Deprecated → Retired. Once a model is marked Deprecated, Anthropic provides a recommended replacement and at least 60 days of notice before retirement. After the retirement date, API calls to that model identifier fail. The table below lists every Claude model deprecation announcement that has been published, drawn from the official Model deprecations page. The Recommended Replacement column reflects the currently recommended successor on Anthropic's deprecation page as of the time of writing. Anthropic updates this recommendation as newer models become available, so for older deprecation announcements the recommended replacement listed here is generally not the model that was suggested at the time of the original announcement. * The table can be sorted by clicking on the column names. Frequently Asked Questions When did Claude 1 launch? Claude 1 was announced together with Claude Instant on March 14, 2023, when Anthropic opened the Anthropic API for early access. See the official Introducing Claude announcement. When did Claude 2 launch? Claude 2 was announced on July 11, 2023, accompanied by the public claude.ai chat interface. See Claude 2 . When did Claude 3 launch? The Claude 3 family (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) was announced together on March 4, 2024. Claude 3 Opus and Claude 3 Sonnet were generally available the same day, and Claude 3 Haiku became generally available on March 13, 2024. See Introducing the next generation of Claude and Claude 3 Haiku - our fastest model yet . When did Claude 3.5 Sonnet launch? Claude 3.5 Sonnet launched on June 20, 2024. An updated revision, sometimes called Claude 3.5 Sonnet (new) or v2, was announced together with Claude 3.5 Haiku and Computer Use on October 22, 2024. See Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Introducing computer use, a new Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Claude 3.5 Haiku . When did Claude 3.7 Sonnet launch? Claude 3.7 Sonnet was announced on February 24, 2025, alongside the Claude Code research preview. It was Anthropic's first hybrid-reasoning model with an extended-thinking mode. See Claude 3.7 Sonnet and Claude Code . When did Claude 4 launch? Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4 launched on May 22, 2025, opening the Claude 4 generation. Claude Code also reached general availability that day. See Introducing Claude 4 . When was Claude Opus 4.7 released? Claude Opus 4.7 was announced on April 16, 2026. It was the frontier Claude model until Claude Opus 4.8 superseded it on May 28, 2026. See Claude Opus 4.7 . When was Claude Opus 4.8 released? Claude Opus 4.8 was announced on May 28, 2026 - roughly 42 days after Opus 4.7, the shortest gap so far between consecutive Claude Opus releases - and was the most capable Opus-tier model until Claude Opus 5 superseded it on July 24, 2026 (Claude Fable 5 had separately introduced the Mythos-class tier above Opus on June 9, 2026). It focuses on honesty and reliability (Anthropic reports it is about four times less likely than Opus 4.7 to let flaws in code it has written pass unremarked), more efficient tool calling, and stronger agentic judgment - including improved computer-use performance (84% on the Online-Mind2Web benchmark) - and it launched alongside the Dynamic Workflows research preview in Claude Code and user-facing effort control in claude.ai and Cowork. It is available on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry under the model identifier claude-opus-4-8 . See Claude Opus 4.8 . When was Claude Opus 5 released? Claude Opus 5 was announced on July 24, 2026 as a step-change improvement over Claude Opus 4.8 and is the most capable Opus-tier model as of the time of writing, described by Anthropic as coming close to Claude Fable 5's frontier intelligence at half the price (Claude Fable 5 remains the frontier model in the Mythos-class tier above Opus). It supports a 1-million-token context window (both the default and the maximum), 128K output tokens, thinking on by default, the full effort ladder including xhigh and max , and a fast mode at around 2.5 times the default speed, and it became the new default model on the Claude Max plan. It launched on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry on announcement day under the model identifier claude-opus-5 . See Introducing Claude Opus 5 . When was Claude Fable 5 released? Claude Fable 5 was announced on June 9, 2026, together with Claude Mythos 5, and is the current Claude frontier model as of the time of writing. It introduced the Mythos-class capability tier above the Opus class and is Anthropic's most capable widely released model, with always-on adaptive thinking, a 1-million-token context window, 128K output tokens, and safety classifiers that automatically fall back to Claude Opus 4.8 for flagged requests. It became generally available on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry the same day under the model identifier claude-fable-5 . See Introducing Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 . Note that on June 12, 2026 Anthropic suspended access to Claude Fable 5 (and Claude Mythos 5) to comply with a US government export-control directive, while keeping all other Claude models available; the directive was later lifted and Anthropic began redeploying Claude Fable 5 globally on July 1, 2026. See the suspension FAQ below. What is Claude Mythos 5 and Project Glasswing? Claude Mythos 5, announced on June 9, 2026 alongside Claude Fable 5, shares Claude Fable 5's capabilities without the safety classifiers. It is not generally available - it is offered in limited availability to approved customers (such as select biology researchers) through Anthropic's Project Glasswing program, with access arranged via Anthropic, AWS, or Google Cloud account teams. Its model identifier is claude-mythos-5 , and it succeeds the earlier invitation-only Claude Mythos Preview. Access to Claude Mythos 5, together with Claude Fable 5, was suspended on June 12, 2026 under a US government directive; see the next question. Why was access to Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 suspended in June 2026? On June 12, 2026, Anthropic announced that it had received a US government export-control directive ordering it to suspend access to Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 for any foreign national - whether inside or outside the United States, and including foreign-national Anthropic employees. Anthropic states that, to comply, it must disable both Mythos-class models for all customers. The government cited a suspected way of bypassing ("jailbreaking") Claude Fable 5's safeguards, reportedly demonstrated by asking the model to read a codebase and fix its software flaws; Anthropic responded that the technique exposed only relatively simple vulnerabilities that are also reachable through other commercially available models, that it disagrees that such a narrow potential jailbreak should warrant recalling a commercial model, and that it is working to restore access as soon as possible. Access to all other Claude models (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) is unaffected. The directive was subsequently lifted, and on June 30, 2026 Anthropic announced that it was redeploying Claude Fable 5 globally (starting July 1, 2026) with updated cybersecurity safeguards - including a new safety classifier that blocks the reported bypass in over 99% of cases - while restoring Claude Mythos 5 access for a set of US organizations; on July 2, 2026 it published further detail on Fable 5's cyber safeguards and a proposed industry framework for scoring jailbreak severity. See Statement on the US government directive to suspend access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 , Redeploying Claude Fable 5 , and More details on Fable 5's cyber safeguards and our jailbreak framework . When was Claude Sonnet 5 released? Claude Sonnet 5 was announced on June 30, 2026 as Anthropic's most capable Sonnet-tier model, bringing near-Opus intelligence to coding, agents, and professional work at Sonnet cost. It is a strict improvement over Claude Sonnet 4.6 across the cost-performance curve and became the default model for the Free and Pro plans. It offers adaptive thinking, the xhigh effort level, higher-resolution vision, a 1-million-token context window, and 128K output tokens, and launched on the Claude API, Claude Code, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry under the model identifier claude-sonnet-5 . See Introducing Claude Sonnet 5 . When did Claude add vision support? Vision (multimodal image input) was added to Claude on March 4, 2024 with the Claude 3 family, and was available on every tier (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) from launch. When did Claude add tool use? Tool use was first introduced as a beta on November 21, 2023 with Claude 2.1, and reached general availability on May 30, 2024 across Claude 3 Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku. See Tool use is now generally available . When did Claude add Computer Use? Computer Use was released as a public beta on October 22, 2024 alongside Claude 3.5 Sonnet (new). See Introducing computer use, a new Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Claude 3.5 Haiku . Claude Haiku 4.5 (October 15, 2025) was the first Haiku-tier model to support Computer Use. When did Claude become available on Amazon Bedrock? Claude 2 became available on Amazon Bedrock at the Bedrock general availability launch on September 28, 2023. The strategic Anthropic + Amazon collaboration was announced three days earlier on September 25, 2023. Since then, every major Claude generation has been made available on Amazon Bedrock either on the day of its Anthropic announcement or within a few weeks. When did Claude become available on Google Cloud Vertex AI? Google Cloud Vertex AI began carrying Claude models on March 20, 2024, when Claude 3 Sonnet and Claude 3 Haiku became generally available on Vertex AI. Claude 3 Opus followed in public preview in April 2024 and reached general availability in June 2024. When did Claude become available on Microsoft Foundry? Microsoft Foundry first carried Claude on November 18, 2025, when Claude Sonnet 4.5, Claude Haiku 4.5, and Claude Opus 4.1 became available in public preview. About a week later, on November 24, 2025, Claude Opus 4.5 launched on Microsoft Foundry on announcement day, simultaneously with the Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock, and Google Cloud Vertex AI. Every subsequent Claude release (Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, Fable 5, Sonnet 5, Opus 5) has continued to ship on Microsoft Foundry on the day of the Anthropic announcement. When was each Claude model deprecated? See the Deprecations and Model Lifecycle section above for the full deprecation table. The most recent deprecation announcement, on June 5, 2026, marks Claude Opus 4.1 for retirement on August 5, 2026. What is the difference between Claude Opus, Claude Sonnet, and Claude Haiku? Since the Claude 3 generation in March 2024, Anthropic has positioned the three tiers as follows. Claude Opus is the maximum-capability tier, used for the hardest reasoning, coding, and agentic tasks. Claude Sonnet is the balanced tier, used for production workloads where cost and latency matter alongside capability. Claude Haiku is the low-latency, low-cost tier, used for high-volume, simpler tasks. Capabilities such as extended thinking and Computer Use originally launched on Sonnet or Opus and have progressively moved down to Haiku - for example, Claude Haiku 4.5 was the first Haiku model with extended thinking and Computer Use. In June 2026, Anthropic added a fourth, Mythos-class tier above Opus, introduced by Claude Fable 5 (generally available) and Claude Mythos 5 (limited availability through Project Glasswing), for the most demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work. Is there a Claude Haiku 4.6, Claude Haiku 4.7, or Claude Haiku 4.8? No. As of July 2026, the most recent Haiku model is Claude Haiku 4.5 from October 15, 2025. Anthropic has not released Haiku versions corresponding to every Sonnet or Opus minor revision. Summary In this article, I built a historical timeline of Anthropic Claude foundation models from Claude 1 in March 2023 through Claude Fable 5 and Claude Sonnet 5 in June 2026 and Claude Opus 5 in July 2026, organized by the model family tree, the major release timeline, the evolution of capabilities, availability across cloud platforms, and the deprecation lifecycle. In three years, Claude has gone from a single proprietary chat model with a 9K-token context window to a four-tier family (the Mythos-class tier with Claude Fable 5, plus Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku) with 1-million-token context windows, native vision, tool use, Computer Use, extended thinking, a persistent memory tool, and availability across the Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry. Within the Opus / Sonnet / Haiku tiers, each generation has consistently shipped at the same or lower price than the previous one - the new Mythos-class tier introduced with Claude Fable 5 in June 2026 instead sits above Opus in both capability and price - and capabilities that originally debuted on the Opus or Sonnet tier - such as Computer Use and extended thinking - have progressively become available on the Haiku tier as well. I will continue to monitor how Anthropic's release cadence and capability roadmap evolve. The most reliable place to track new Claude model announcements is the official Anthropic News page, with model deprecations listed on the official Model deprecations page. In addition, there are also related history-and-timeline articles on hidekazu-konishi.com, so please have a look if you are interested. Applications relying on Anthropic models may need occasional updates to keep working. Impacted customers will always be notified by email and in the documentation. This page lists all API deprecations, along with recommended replacements.  Overview Anthropic uses the following terms to describe the model lifecycle: Active: The model is fully supported and recommended for use. Legacy: The model will no longer receive updates and may be deprecated in the future. Deprecated: The model is still functional but no longer recommended. Anthropic provides a recommended replacement and assigns a retirement date. Retired: The model is no longer available for use. Requests to retired models will fail.  Deprecated models are likely to be less reliable than active models. Move workloads to active models to maintain the highest level of support and reliability. The dates on this page apply to Anthropic-operated platforms: the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS , and Microsoft Foundry . Partner-operated platforms (Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud) set their own retirement schedules, so a model's lifecycle status and dates can differ. See the Amazon Bedrock , Amazon Bedrock (Opus 4.6 and earlier) , and Google Cloud model tables.  Migrating to replacements Once a model is deprecated, migrate all usage to a suitable replacement before the retirement date. Requests to models past the retirement date will fail. To help measure the performance of replacement models on your tasks, consider thorough testing of your applications with the new models well before the retirement date. For specific instructions on migrating to the latest Claude models, see the Migration guide .  Notifications Anthropic notifies customers with active deployments for models with upcoming retirements, providing at least 60 days' notice before model retirement for publicly released models.  Auditing model usage To help identify usage of deprecated models, customers can access an audit of their API usage. Follow these steps: Go to the Usage page in Claude Console. Click Export . Review the downloaded CSV to see usage broken down by API key and model. This audit will help you locate any instances where your application is still using deprecated models, allowing you to prioritize updates to newer models before the retirement date.  Best practices Regularly check the documentation for updates on model deprecations. Test your applications with newer models well before the retirement date of your current model. Update your code to use the recommended replacement model as soon as possible. Contact the support team if you need assistance with migration or have any questions.  Deprecation downsides and mitigations Anthropic currently deprecates and retires models to ensure capacity for new model releases. This comes with downsides: Users who value specific models must migrate to new versions Researchers lose access to models for ongoing and comparative studies Model retirement introduces safety- and model welfare-related risks At some point, Anthropic hopes to make past models publicly available again. In the meantime, Anthropic has committed to long-term preservation of model weights and other measures to help mitigate these impacts. For more details, see Commitments on Model Deprecation and Preservation .  Model status  Claude Mythos Preview ( claude-mythos-preview ) is deprecated. To migrate to Claude Mythos 5 ( claude-mythos-5 ), see the migration guide . ## Model Description (Claude 3 Sonnet)
The balanced mid-tier model of the Claude 3 generation, offering strong capabilities at an efficient price point.
